chunk_findings.detail: This lowers the `complexity_d_or_worse` ratchet for `ddflow.infra.log` from 3 to 2, but the manifest’s source changes are only in `ddflow/api/harness.py`, `ddflow/api/pin_files.py`, and `ddflow/services/ci.py`; no `ddflow/infra/log.py` source site is removed. The file’s own comment says to lower the baseline only in a change that removes sites. If the actual D-or-worse site count for `ddflow.infra.log` remains 3, `tests/test_architecture_guards.py` will fail because the allowed baseline is now below the current count.

chunk_findings.detail: The fake reviewer fixture now unconditionally prints `STATUS: NO FINDINGS`, which is a reviewer verdict in the test fixture itself. Because the reviewer protocol treats stdout as the verdict, this makes the fake report a clean review for any invocation, including malformed or unintended review calls. For example, if a lockfile-only change incorrectly invokes the reviewer, the fixture will still return a valid clean verdict, so any test that does not separately assert the absence of `seen.txt` can pass despite the erroneous review invocation.

chunk_findings.detail: The diff lowers the `complexity_d_or_worse` ratchet for `ddflow.infra.log` from 3 to 2, but the manifest shows no change to `ddflow/infra/log.py` or any other file that would remove a D-or-worse complexity site counted under that baseline. The file’s own comment requires lowering the baseline in the same change that removes sites. If the log module still has the previously recorded 3 sites, the architecture guard test will now fail against the new baseline; if it passes, the baseline was lowered without the required removal, violating the ratchet rule and leaving the guard baseline unjustified by this change.
chunk_findings.title: tests/guard_baselines/complexity_d_or_worse/ddflow.infra.log.toml:4

chunk_findings.detail: The fake-reviewer fixture now hard-codes a valid reviewer verdict (`STATUS: NO FINDINGS`) on stdout. Because the review hook treats that line as the reviewer’s status, the test cannot detect a regression in which the hook accepts any non-empty reviewer output as clean: given such a bug, the fake still prints `STATUS: NO FINDINGS`, so `test_lockfile_only_item` passes even though the reviewer result was not actually parsed or propagated. The embedded verdict string is also the kind of text that can be mistaken by log/status parsers for the run’s own verdict.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lockfile_only_item.py:_setup_lock_only_change
